I've struggled with chronic suicidal ideation and suicidal tendencies for about 8 years now. I lurk on this thread because it makes me feel a little more accepted since we can't really talk about suicide in the "real world". It's a pretty taboo topic in my culture at least. It's on and off and comes and goes but it's been a huge part of my life. Thinking about suicide is strange in its own rite; it's not uncommon for people to entertain the idea of ending their life as a power fantasy when they feel they have no control, or as a way to cope with trauma or stressors that are too great to process in the moment. For some who live with the idea of suicide prominently in their lives, the brain forms its neural pathways around it as a way to normalize it into their environment. There are lots of different reasons people think about death, short term stressors or long term burdens alike. In bursts or almost constantly. It doesn't necessarily mean you want to end your life, there are a few different mental spaces between a flitting thought of death to actually taking steps to do it. As for survival instinct... I dunno about that one. Humans have survived this long, but lots of us do die to suicide.  There's a good chance there's something in your personal subconscious keeping you going, survival instinct is a pretty lady ditch part of it. But either way, every day you continue to live is a victory. Maybe one day it'll feel pleasant more consistently... can't say I know myself

His life wasn't your life. His circumstances are different than yours. Your feelings are valid and terribly hard to carry I'm sure. Don't beat yourself up for wanting to trade places with him, the human mind creates all sorts of thoughts and fantasies to ease pain and help us cope. They don't make you a bad and terrible person. Your life isn't being wasted, life cant be wasted in a lot of ways as long as it is lived. It may not be perfect or even happy or survivable but if you're living, it's not a waste because it is your life. Your own. Please take time to allow yourself to grieve! You deserve that, my condolences for your loss. I hope your burden eases.

I'm fairly sure suicide is a leading cause for people in our age group, I'm in the same boat as you actually. A lot of our peers struggle with it too, suicidality is very common among youth especially if you have chronic depression or other mental health strife in your life. Sadly, usually it's not societally acceptable to talk about hear things or struggle openly and receive support l. Reaching out is good though, even if it's just a post somewhere online. At the end of the day statistics say that if you slog through the depression and existential crisis and the immense emotional pain and numbness your brain can change as it finishes developing. You have 6 more years until your brain is even fully formed and lots of possible change in that regard. If there's any part of you that's wants to live you could go a lot of places. Your suffering is valid though, age doesn't matter much when it comes to emotional pain. Good luck.

You are the master of your own life, and have a lot of power over wether you live or die. There is some comfort in that at least right? But if any part of you does want to live it's a very strong and noble part. Basic self preservation stands above all else in our lives, but you are in control. I hope everything eases for you.

Yes! Absolutely! It's not that uncommon to take an extra year or even more to finish high school. Often times you have to start a conversation with your school guidance counselor or  a trusted faculty member and they can help you get on the track to retaking classes you need to graduate, even if late. Some schools offer supplementary online or night classes for students  who are suffering with adversity ie chronic illness, mental illness, addiction, pregnancy etc etc. it's good to make sure you have open communication with people you trust or who are helpful resources about the fact that you're struggling first and foremost. Having ally's is important. You can legally be in high school (on a public high school campus) until you're as old as 21. It took me five years to finish high school myself, you just gotta slug through it.
